paragraphs.text: The semi-legendary Inca-Chanka war between Cusco and the Chanka chiefdom is dated 1401 CE to 1500 CE, at an approximate location.
A Battle of Cusco is recorded in 1438, placed approximately.
Túpac Inca Yupanqui was born here in 1441, Manco Inca in 1500, and Túpac Huallpa in 1510, all at approximate locations.
In 1533 a Battle of Cusco was fought between the Spanish Conquistadors and forces of the Incas, and battles at Anta and Capi, placed approximately, date to that year.
In 1536 Manco Inca Yupanqui led an Incan army in a 10-month siege of Cusco, held by Spanish conquistadors and Indian auxiliaries under Hernando Pizarro.
Sacsayhuaman and Yucay saw battles in 1536, at approximate locations.
In 1537 Hernando Pizarro led the besieged in a raid on the emperor's headquarters at Ollantaytambo.
The Incans hoped the siege would restore their empire, but it was ultimately unsuccessful.
In 1538 Hernando and Gonzalo Pizarro fought rival conquistador Diego de Almagro at the Battle of Las Salinas.
Inca Garcilaso de la Vega, later a chronicler, was born here in 1539, at an approximate location.
In 1548 Gonzalo Pizarro and Pedro de la Gasca fought the Battle of Jaquijahuana, during the Revolt of the Encomenderos.
The Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire ended in Spanish victory in 1572 and colonization of the region as the Viceroyalty of Peru.
